A_target.statement:
Let $M$ be a [[Definition:Compact Manifold|compact]] [[Definition:Oriented Manifold|oriented]] [[Definition:Smooth Manifold|smooth]] $n$-manifold with boundary, and $\omega$ a [[Definition:Differential Form|differential $\paren {n - 1}$-form]] on $M$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \int_M \d \omega = \int_{\partial M} \omega$

B_source.statement:
Let $f$ be [[Definition:Continuously Differentiable|continuously differentiable]] on $\closedint a b$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \int_a^b \map {f'} x \rd x = \map f b - \map f a$

derived.f(b)-f(a) (evaluation on the boundary): integral of omega over boundary M

object_map.reformulation: Reinterpret differentiation as the exterior derivative and 'evaluate at endpoints' as 'integrate over the boundary', so FTC becomes the 1-dimensional case of a general boundary law.

validity_conditions: The interval [a,b] is a 1-manifold whose oriented boundary is {b} minus {a}; FTC is exactly Stokes in dimension 1.
The generalization is genuine new content (exterior calculus, orientation, manifolds), not a renaming - so this is generalization, not transport.
M must be a compact oriented smooth manifold with boundary and omega a smooth form for the general statement.
proof_plan: The [[Fundamental Theorem of Calculus]] relates the integral of a derivative to evaluation on the boundary $\set {a, b}$.
Abstract the derivative to the [[Definition:Exterior Derivative|exterior derivative]] $\d$, and the endpoints to the oriented boundary $\partial M$.
